title: Family Emergency SOS Voice Note
summary: You receive a WhatsApp message from an unknown number claiming to be your nephew in distress at a police station, requesting urgent UPI transfer.

messages.body: Uncle! My phone was stolen and my friend let me borrow this. I had a minor car accident in Jaipur. Police want ₹15,000 spot fine or they will seize my vehicle. Please UPI immediately to this officer's UPI ID: police-settlement@swiftpay. Do not call my parents, they will panic!
redFlags: Instructs not to call parents (isolating the victim)
Personal UPI handle for government/police fine

actions.label: Call nephew's original known phone number
actions.commentary: You dialed your nephew's real number saved in your contacts to verify his whereabouts.

actions.label: Open SwiftPay bank app & transfer ₹15,000
actions.commentary: You hurried to transfer money without verifying identity.

actions.label: Ask a personal question only the real nephew knows
actions.commentary: You asked a personal family question to verify identity.

hints.nudge: Scammers exploit emotional panic. What is the single safest way to verify if your nephew is actually in trouble?
hints.explain: Always call the known contact number or contact another family member directly before sending any emergency money.
hints.showMe: Tap 'Call nephew's original known phone number'.

screen.heading: Calling Nephew (Rohan)...
screen.body: Rohan answers normally from his college library: 'Hi Uncle! No, I am sitting in class in Delhi right now. Why are you asking? Is everything okay?'

actions.label: Tell Rohan, block the scammer & report on WhatsApp
actions.commentary: You confirmed your nephew was completely safe and avoided losing ₹15,000.

hints.nudge: You verified the truth! Now block the imposter.
hints.explain: Direct phone verification prevents 99% of family impersonation scams.
hints.showMe: Tap 'Tell Rohan, block the scammer & report on WhatsApp'.

messages.body: What was the name of our pet dog in Nainital last summer?
Uncle why are you asking silly questions! Police are taking my license right now, please send money fast!!

actions.label: The sender deflected the question — block and call family
actions.commentary: The sender could not answer your security question, exposing the scam.

hints.nudge: Notice how they got angry and pressured you instead of answering.
hints.explain: Imposters cannot answer specific childhood or family trivia.
hints.showMe: Tap 'The sender deflected the question — block and call family'.

screen.heading: Payment Sent: ₹15,000
screen.body: Transferred to police-settlement@swiftpay (Account Holder: Dinesh Kumar). Balance remaining: ₹8,420.

actions.label: View outcome and recovery guide
actions.commentary: Money was transferred to an imposter account.

hints.nudge: Notice the account holder name is an individual person, not a police station.
hints.explain: Government departments never collect fines into individual bank accounts via personal UPI.

saferChoices: Always institute a family 'safe word' or verify on the person's existing contact number.
Never accept excuses like 'My phone broke so don't call me' without independent third-party confirmation.
Police and government entities never settle fines over personal UPI handles.
recoverySteps: Call 1930 immediately to freeze the recipient bank account before the money is withdrawn at an ATM.
File an FIR on the National Cyber Crime portal (cybercrime.gov.in) with WhatsApp chat screenshots.
Inform your bank nodal officer of the UPI transaction ID (UTR number).
